BUDGET CUTS Canary in the Coalmine

By: Marion Edmunds | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We show how national budget cuts will cripple delivery in the public service

Unique Selling Point:
This is an unreported story but will have devastating consequences on the ground where people will not get services in health, education and social services as a result of the freezing of posts and the cutting of budgets which were unfunded.

Summary:
The National Government concluded a wage agreement with Public Servants last year which was greater than the government could afford. As a result the treasury has passed that shortfall down to the provincial governments, so increased the wages of the civil servants but not provided the provincial paymasters with the cash to fund that increase. As a result the provinces are scrambling to cut budgets and are doing that by slashing personnel numbers, plunging service delivery into crisis. We talk to a doctor and his patients on the one hand that has been affected by this and a teacher who has lost her job and is now lost to the education system and then test their views against the political heads in the Western Cape of how they are handling it. This unreported story has been present in news pages, but because the Western Cape is the only one complaining and possibly threatening an InterGovernmental Dispute they are the canary in the coalmine in terms of what will happen in other provinces.

Press Release:


Canary in the Coal Mine
Last year, national government signed off on a public servants wage agreement that the country simply couldn’t afford. Under pressure from trade unions, government increased its already overburdened wage bill, pushing the cost of the shortfall onto provincial budgets. Now provinces have been forced to cut their budgets, slashing personnel numbers and plunging service delivery further into crisis. Already overstretched, the public health and education sectors in the Western Cape have been dealt a devastating blow, and they’re not afraid to say it. Carte Blanche examines the developing crisis and asks: is the Western Cape the canary in the coal mine?
Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Govan Whittles

Script:


BUDGET CUTS #6622
FINAL DRAFT

(VO 1) THERE’S A CRISIS PLAYING OUT INSIDE CLINICS AND HOSPITALS…

DR KGOSI LETLAPE
MP: ActionSA
Our public Health care scenario has basically become a crime scene.

(VO 2) A TRAGEDY IS TAKING SHAPE BEHIND SCHOOL GATES….

SIVIWE GWARUBE
Minister for Basic Education: GNU
We're no longer just trimming the fat. We are right at the bone.

(VO 3) SEVERE BUDGET CUTS ARE PUSHING PROFESSIONALS ON THE FRONTLINE TO DESPAIR…

DAVID MAYNIER
MEC for Education: Western Cape
The scale of the cuts were just simply too great for provinces to absorb.

AIMEE VENTER
High School Teacher: Natural Sciences
It is still very raw. I am still angry.

(VO 4) A WORKFORCE OF OVER A MILLION GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES IS CALLING FOR A DECENT WAGE …

(VO 5) WHILE SERVICE DELIVERY IS STUMBLING WITH NO RELIEF IN SIGHT….

(VO 6) AIMEE VENTER HAS SPENT ALMOST HALF HER LIFE TEACHING IN THE WESTERN CAPE
THIS YEAR SHE’S BEEN ON CONTRACT AS A NATURAL SCIENCE TEACHER IN A TOWNSHIP SCHOOL

AIMEE VENTER
Teacher: Natural Sciences
There's a massive need for teachers trained properly in teaching Natural Sciences and to teach learners how to think critically and without someone to lead them, they're not going to just naturally develop it.

(VO 7) BUT SHE’S RECEIVED A LETTER TO SAY THAT FROM JANUARY SHE WILL NO LONGER HAVE A JOB.

AIMEE VENTER
Teacher: Natural Sciences
I was in utter disbelief. I literally started crying. I thought science teachers would always have a job, and now suddenly I'm sitting in a position where that certainty has been taken away from me….

(VO 8) VENTER IS ONE OF MANY TEACHERS IN THE WESTERN CAPE WHOSE POSTS HAVE BEEN CUT.
SHE’S SPOKEN OUT - HASHTAG I AM ONE OF THE 2400

AIMEE VENTER
Teacher: Natural Sciences
I wanted to put a face to the teachers to show that we are people. We have faces, we have families. We have a passion for education. We're not just a number.

(VO 9) BUT DECISION-MAKERS SAY THEY ARE FORCED TO TREAT THOUSANDS OF PUBLIC SECTOR PROFESSIONALS AS NUMBERS, AS THEY TRY TO BALANCE THE BOOKS.

NATIONAL GOVERNMENT ALLOCATES MONEY ANNUALLY TO PROVINCES TO SPEND ON SERVICE DELIVERY.

EACH PROVINCE THEN PRIORITISES SPENDING IN ITS OWN BUDGETS.

BUT LAST YEAR, THE STATE NEGOTIATED A NATIONAL WAGE INCREASE WITH PUBLIC SERVANTS WHICH EXCEEDED EXPECTATIONS.

FORCING THE PROVINCES TO DRAMATICALLY DOWNSIZE SPENDING PLANS.

PTC: Govan Whittles The fact is public service unions negotiated a higher wage increase than the state can afford, and now the provinces are paying for it.

DAVID MAYNIER
MEC for Education: Western Cape
The situation is, in fact, probably even more severe than many people realize.
Our province is a province where we expect net enrollment to increase in 2025 by anything up to 14,000 learners.

GOVAN: You're expecting more learners, but you have fewer teachers?

DM: Correct.

DAVID MAYNIER
MEC for Education: Western Cape
14,000 additional learners is roughly the equivalent of 14 additional schools in one school year. So the pressure in the Western Cape is enormous.

(VO10) DAVID MAYNIER IS THE MEC FOR EDUCATION.
HIS HEADACHE IS A 3-POINT-8 BILLION RAND HOLE IN THE SCHOOLS BUDGET OVER THREE YEARS.
ACROSS ALL GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS, THE WESTERN CAPE IS A CASE-STUDY IN CRISIS MANAGEMENT…
BY SPEAKING OUT, IT’S THE CANARY IN THE COALMINE AS OTHER PROVINCIAL ADMINISTRATIONS ARE ALSO IN TROUBLE.

DAVID MAYNIER
MEC for Education: Western Cape
It is a shared problem. Other provinces are starting to cut spending, for example, on school nutrition, on learner transport, on transfers to schools. Many provinces have stopped paying suppliers, stopped paying municipalities and some provinces are set to dramatically overspend in this financial year.

(VO 11) AUSTERITY IS HITTING VERY HARD - AS NATIONAL TREASURY PLEADS POVERTY.

PTC GOVAN WHITTLES:It's difficult to get a clear idea of how each provincial administration is adapting to these budget cuts. It's a mixed picture, pinching here, scraping there, or slicing services to the bone, and sometimes losing them all together.

(VO 12) THE STRAIN ISN’T LIMITED TO EDUCATION. HEALTH IS FEELING THE SQUEEZE TOO.
THE OPHTHALMOLOGY DEPARTMENT AT GROOTE SCHUUR HOSPITAL IS NOW UNDERSTAFFED.
PIONEERING EYE SURGEON DR HAMZAH MUSTAK RESIGNED LAST YEAR, AS PART OF A SUCCESSION PLAN TO GIVE A JUNIOR A CHANCE TO SKILL UP IN HIS SPECIALITY.
BUT THE HOSPITAL MADE A SAVING INSTEAD.

PROFESSOR HAMZAH MUSTAK
Ophthalmologist: Specialist in ocular oncology
There was only one post, really in the entire country, for the eye cancer specialist. Since freezing the post, there is no one who can see eye cancer patients actually.

(VO 13) CARTE BLANCHE FIRST MET PROFESSOR MUSTAK IN 2018 WHEN HE WAS PART OF A TEAM DEVELOPING INNOVATIVE METHODS IN HIGHLY SPECIALISED SURGERY.
DESPITE RESIGNING TO MOVE INTO THE PRIVATE SECTOR, HE VOLUNTEERS TO ASSIST LESS EXPERIENCED DOCTORS WHO ARE HANDLING AN INCREASED WORKLOAD.

PROFESSOR HAMZAH MUSTAK
Opthalmologist: Specialist in ocular oncology
On the days that I come to clinic, there are over 40 patients waiting to be seen by me . …they don't have a diagnosis, they don't have a treatment plan, so spending three entire whole days at the government hospital without even knowing what's wrong with them and what the plan is for them,

GOVAN WHITTLES: What’s been your experience with the budget cuts in the health sector? Is it difficult to talk about it?

PROFESSOR HAMZAH MUSTAK
Opthalmologist: Specialist in ocular oncology
I think the frustration is that it's not something that's in my control yet, I'm the one who has to explain to the patients what the situation is.

(VO 14) THE BELT-TIGHTENING IMPACTS ON PROF MUSTAK’s FORMER PATIENTS.
CAPETONIAN ZADONISA MC KENZIE HAS A CHRONIC EYE CONDITION.

ZADONISA MC KENZIE
Patient: Groote Schuur Hospital
My right cornea is hanging on a string. If I don't get treatment, I can be blind.

(VO 15) MC KENZIE HAS WAITED FOR ALMOST A YEAR FOR A CRITICAL OPERATION

ZADONISA MC KENZIE
Patient: Groote Schuur Hospital
They don't have the specialists available. And I feel the MEC of Health with the government, has failed the patients of Groote Schuur. I've experienced a drop in the quality.

PTC GOVAN WHITTLES: South Africa has world class operating theatres, the iconic Groote Schuur Hospital being case in point, but this is precisely where the impact of the budget cuts is being felt.

(VO 16) FREEZING POSTS HAS LED TO A REDUCED NUMBER OF STAFFED OPERATING THEATRES, RESULTING IN 40 FEWER SURGERIES WEEKLY COMPARED TO LAST YEAR.
OVER 4-AND-A HALF THOUSAND PEOPLE ARE CURRENTLY WAITING FOR SURGERY AT GROOTE SCHUUR HOSPITAL, OF WHICH TEN PER CENT ARE CANCER PATIENTS.

PROFESSOR HAMZAH MUSTAK
Ophthalmologist: Specialist in ocular oncology
I coined the term theatre load shedding, … because we have lost anaesthetists whose posts haven't been filled, they've been frozen. …Without them, we cannot perform surgeries because you can't give a general anesthetic. We are also short of nursing staff.

(VO 17) THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT SAID THIS WEEK THAT THEY ARE IN THE PROCESS OF FILLING PROF MUSTAK’S POST IN A CAMPAIGN TO REBUILD LOST CAPACITY.

MIREILLE WENGER
MEC for Health: Western Cape
We have had to close some theaters across the province as a result of the budget cuts,

(VO 18) BUT THE MEC FOR HEALTH MIREILLE WEGNER SAYS THE QUALITY OF HEALTH CARE IS NOT COMPROMISED - JUST THE QUANTITY.

MIREILLE WENGER
MEC for Health: Western Cape
I mean you can't have a half staffed theatre, so we're making sure that the theatres that are operational are fully staffed and have all the equipment that they need for those procedures for patient safety. We're now up to a backlog of about 83,000 surgeries.

GOVAN WHITTLES: Are those life threatening surgeries?

MIREILLE WENGER: It ranges from the very minor to the more urgent.

(VO 19) THE FINANCIAL CRISIS EXACERBATED BY THE 2023 WAGE AGREEMENT HAS DISRUPTED THE BEST-LAID PLANS OF PROVINCIAL DEPARTMENTS ACROSS THE COUNTRY.

DAVID MAYNIER
MEC for Education: Western Cape
Sometime in June 2023 … I remember the day where, as a result of the expected budget deficit and the fiscal uncertainty, I cancelled 11 school builds in a day.

MIREILLE WENGER
MEC for Health: Western Cape
Traditionally, wage deals were fully funded, and that's what made that particular financial year significant in that the funding didn't follow, following the negotiation of the wage deal.

GOVAN WHITTLES: How much was the wage? Was the wage bill for this?
MEC: So we were looking at a pressure of just over a billion rand, and we got 70% of that. So we're looking at about….
GOVAN WHITTLES: 300 million.
MEC: Yeah,
GOVAN: The short fall?
MEC: Big numbers, yeah.

(VO 20) IN OTHER WORDS, THE PROVINCIAL DEPARTMENT FEELS IT’S HANDS HAVE BEEN TIED BY A SPENDING DECISION TAKEN AT NATIONAL LEVEL.
IN PARLIAMENT, OPPOSITION POLITICIAN DR KGOSI LETLAPE IS ASKING TOUGH QUESTIONS ABOUT THE IMPACT ON THE HEALTH SYSTEM.

DR KGOSI LETLAPE
MP: ActionSA
Basically cutting budgets to a struggling system like we have is violating the constitutional rights of patients.

(VO 21) DR LETLAPE SAYS NOTHING WILL CHANGE UNTIL ALL PUBLIC SERVANTS AND POLITICIANS ARE COMPELLED TO USE STATE HEALTH CARE, RATHER THAN PRIVATE.

DR KGOSI LETLAPE
MP: ActionSA
We can't be talking about the wage bill when the President has the temerity to go and double the size of cabinet.. …, you know, for ordinary people that are essential, that make an impact on ordinary lives, that's where we cut. But for things that are grandiose, political agreements, we will spend lavishly without any restraint. It doesn't make sense.

Siviwe Gwarube Sound up: And to perform the functions of my office conscientiously and to the best of my ability…

(VO 22) ONE OF THE NEWCOMERS TO CABINET IS THE MINISTER OF BASIC EDUCATION.
ONCE IN OPPOSITION, SIVIWE GWARUBE IS NOW GRAPPLING WITH A MASSIVE BUDGET CRISIS JUST MONTHS INTO THE JOB.

SIVIWE GWARUBE
Minister for Basic Education: GNU
The figure that gives me chills and and it's not a final figure, but out of about almost 118 billion rand shortfall in the next three years if the budget remains the same.

PTC GOVAN WHITTLES: Ministers are lobbying the Treasury for more cash for service delivery, so there is much anticipation as this week the finance minister prepares to table his spending plan for the next three years.

(VO 23) GWARUBE HAS ORGANISED MEETINGS BETWEEN PROVINCIAL EDUCATION MECs AND TREASURY TO PLEAD THE CASE FOR EDUCATION.
EACH PROVINCE IS MANAGING THEIR BUDGET SHORTFALLS IN THEIR OWN WAY, BUT THIS IS A UNITED CALL FOR HELP.

SIVIWE GWARUBE
Minister for Basic Education: GNU
My plea to Treasury is to say we need immediate buffering of the budget cuts now.

(VO 24) TREASURY TOLD US THEY REGULARLY ADVISE PROVINCES ON HOW BEST TO ALLOCATE THEIR LIMITED MONEY.
ALL EYES WILL BE ON THE FINANCE MINISTER THIS WEEK TO SEE WHAT HE CONCEDES WHEN HE PRESENTS HIS MEDIUM-TERM BUDGET IN PARLIAMENT.
HOW WILL HE BALANCE THE NEEDS OF THE PEOPLE AGAINST THE PAY OF THE PUBLIC SERVANTS?

SIVIWE GWARUBE
Minister for Basic Education: GNU
My view, is education, healthcare, police, service, delivery. Those are the things that are critical to any nation. So we need to have a whole review of government spending so that we can actually put our money where our mouth is. We can’t say these are priorities but then we are putting our money elsewhere.

(VO 25) BUT POLITICAL TALK SEEMS CHEAP TO VENTER AND PROF MUSTAK, BOTH OF WHOM HAVE GIVEN THEIR BEST YEARS TO PUBLIC SERVICE, TO BUILD THE COUNTRY FOR GENERATIONS TO COME.

PROFESSOR HAMZAH MUSTAK
Ophthalmologist: Specialist in ocular oncology
The wait times are what’s longer so explain that to a patient who has eye cancer or any cancer. They can lose their life.

AIMEE VENTER
Teacher: Natural Sciences
I want other teachers to raise their voices. I want them to speak up about what is right and what is wrong. I want them to try to make a difference.

ENDSIT

PRESENTER LINK TO CAMERA:

PROMO 1:
DR KGOSI LETLAPE
MP: ActionSA
Our public Health care scenario has basically become a crime scene,

(VO) THERE’S NONE SO BLIND AS THOSE THAT WILL NOT SEE

ZADONISA MC KENZIE
Patient: Groote Schuur Hospital
Healthcare that is a necessity. Education is necessity. So I feel that the government is to blame big time.

PROMO 2:

PROFESSOR HAMZAH MUSTAK
Ophthalmologist: Specialist in ocular oncology
To see the service that you've built up, you know, taken apart is..

(VO) PROFESSIONALS ON THE FRONTLINE ARE UNDER PRESSURE

AIMEE VENTER
Teacher: Natural Sciences
cutting teacher jobs is completely illogical….You are going to be constantly crowd controlling.

PROMO 3:

(VO) BUDGETS SLASHED, PROGRESS HALTED.
DAVID MAYNIER
MEC for Education: Western Cape
I remember the day where.... I cancelled 11 school builds in a day.

SIVIWE GWARUBE
Minister for Basic Education: GNU
The future of these 13 and a half million children is in jeopardy

(VO) WHO WILL AUSTERITY HURT MOST?
AIMEE VENTER
Teacher: Natural Sciences
It’s still very raw. I am still angry.

DAVID MAYNIER MEC for Education: Western Cape 14,000 additional learners is roughly the equivalent of 14 additional schools in one school year. So the pressure in the Western Cape is enormous. (VO10) DAVID MAYNIER IS THE MEC FOR EDUCATION. HIS HEADACHE IS A 3-POINT-8 BILLION RAND HOLE IN THE SCHOOLS BUDGET OVER THREE YEARS. ACROSS ALL GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS, THE WESTERN CAPE IS A CASE-STUDY IN CRISIS MANAGEMENT… BY SPEAKING OUT, IT’S THE CANARY IN THE COALMINE AS OTHER PROVINCIAL ADMINISTRATIONS ARE ALSO IN TROUBLE. DAVID MAYNIER MEC for Education: Western Cape It is a shared problem. Other provinces are starting to cut spending, for example, on school nutrition, on learner transport, on transfers to schools. Many provinces have stopped paying suppliers, stopped paying municipalities and some provinces are set to dramatically overspend in this financial year. (VO 11) AUSTERITY IS HITTING VERY HARD - AS NATIONAL TREASURY PLEADS POVERTY. PTC GOVAN WHITTLES:It's difficult to get a clear idea of how each provincial administration is adapting to these budget cuts. It's a mixed picture, pinching here, scraping there, or slicing services to the bone, and sometimes losing them all together. (VO 12) THE STRAIN ISN’T LIMITED TO EDUCATION. HEALTH IS FEELING THE SQUEEZE TOO. THE OPHTHALMOLOGY DEPARTMENT AT GROOTE SCHUUR HOSPITAL IS NOW UNDERSTAFFED. PIONEERING EYE SURGEON DR HAMZAH MUSTAK RESIGNED LAST YEAR, AS PART OF A SUCCESSION PLAN TO GIVE A JUNIOR A CHANCE TO SKILL UP IN HIS SPECIALITY. BUT THE HOSPITAL MADE A SAVING INSTEAD. PROFESSOR HAMZAH MUSTAK Ophthalmologist: Specialist in ocular oncology There was only one post, really in the entire country, for the eye cancer specialist. Since freezing the post, there is no one who can see eye cancer patients actually. (VO 13) CARTE BLANCHE FIRST MET PROFESSOR MUSTAK IN 2018 WHEN HE WAS PART OF A TEAM DEVELOPING INNOVATIVE METHODS IN HIGHLY SPECIALISED SURGERY. DESPITE RESIGNING TO MOVE INTO THE PRIVATE SECTOR, HE VOLUNTEERS TO ASSIST LESS EXPERIENCED DOCTORS WHO ARE HANDLING AN INCREASED WORKLOAD. PROFESSOR HAMZAH MUSTAK Opthalmologist: Specialist in ocular oncology On the days that I come to clinic, there are over 40 patients waiting to be seen by me . …they don't have a diagnosis, they don't have a treatment plan, so spending three entire whole days at the government hospital without even knowing what's wrong with them and what the plan is for them, GOVAN WHITTLES: What’s been your experience with the budget cuts in the health sector? Is it difficult to talk about it? PROFESSOR HAMZAH MUSTAK Opthalmologist: Specialist in ocular oncology I think the frustration is that it's not something that's in my control yet, I'm the one who has to explain to the patients what the situation is. (VO 14) THE BELT-TIGHTENING IMPACTS ON PROF MUSTAK’s FORMER PATIENTS. CAPETONIAN ZADONISA MC KENZIE HAS A CHRONIC EYE CONDITION. ZADONISA MC KENZIE Patient: Groote Schuur Hospital My right cornea is hanging on a string. If I don't get treatment, I can be blind. (VO 15) MC KENZIE HAS WAITED FOR ALMOST A YEAR FOR A CRITICAL OPERATION ZADONISA MC KENZIE Patient: Groote Schuur Hospital They don't have the specialists available. And I feel the MEC of Health with the government, has failed the patients of Groote Schuur. I've experienced a drop in the quality. PTC GOVAN WHITTLES: South Africa has world class operating theatres, the iconic Groote Schuur Hospital being case in point, but this is precisely where the impact of the budget cuts is being felt. (VO 16) FREEZING POSTS HAS LED TO A REDUCED NUMBER OF STAFFED OPERATING THEATRES, RESULTING IN 40 FEWER SURGERIES WEEKLY COMPARED TO LAST YEAR. OVER 4-AND-A HALF THOUSAND PEOPLE ARE CURRENTLY WAITING FOR SURGERY AT GROOTE SCHUUR HOSPITAL, OF WHICH TEN PER CENT ARE CANCER PATIENTS. PROFESSOR HAMZAH MUSTAK Ophthalmologist: Specialist in ocular oncology I coined the term theatre load shedding, … because we have lost anaesthetists whose posts haven't been filled, they've been frozen. …Without them, we cannot perform surgeries because you can't give a general anesthetic. We are also short of nursing staff. (VO 17) THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT SAID THIS WEEK THAT THEY ARE IN THE PROCESS OF FILLING PROF MUSTAK’S POST IN A CAMPAIGN TO REBUILD LOST CAPACITY. MIREILLE WENGER MEC for Health: Western Cape We have had to close some theaters across the province as a result of the budget cuts, (VO 18) BUT THE MEC FOR HEALTH MIREILLE WEGNER SAYS THE QUALITY OF HEALTH CARE IS NOT COMPROMISED - JUST THE QUANTITY. MIREILLE WENGER MEC for Health: Western Cape I mean you can't have a half staffed theatre, so we're making sure that the theatres that are operational are fully staffed and have all the equipment that they need for those procedures for patient safety. We're now up to a backlog of about 83,000 surgeries. GOVAN WHITTLES: Are those life threatening surgeries? MIREILLE WENGER: It ranges from the very minor to the more urgent. (VO 19) THE FINANCIAL CRISIS EXACERBATED BY THE 2023 WAGE AGREEMENT HAS DISRUPTED THE BEST-LAID PLANS OF PROVINCIAL DEPARTMENTS ACROSS THE COUNTRY. DAVID MAYNIER MEC for Education: Western Cape Sometime in June 2023 … I remember the day where, as a result of the expected budget deficit and the fiscal uncertainty, I cancelled 11 school builds in a day. MIREILLE WENGER MEC for Health: Western Cape Traditionally, wage deals were fully funded, and that's what made that particular financial year significant in that the funding didn't follow, following the negotiation of the wage deal. GOVAN WHITTLES: How much was the wage? Was the wage bill for this? MEC: So we were looking at a pressure of just over a billion rand, and we got 70% of that. So we're looking at about…. GOVAN WHITTLES: 300 million. MEC: Yeah, GOVAN: The short fall? MEC: Big numbers, yeah. (VO 20) IN OTHER WORDS, THE PROVINCIAL DEPARTMENT FEELS IT’S HANDS HAVE BEEN TIED BY A SPENDING DECISION TAKEN AT NATIONAL LEVEL. IN PARLIAMENT, OPPOSITION POLITICIAN DR KGOSI LETLAPE IS ASKING TOUGH QUESTIONS ABOUT THE IMPACT ON THE HEALTH SYSTEM. DR KGOSI LETLAPE MP: ActionSA Basically cutting budgets to a struggling system like we have is violating the constitutional rights of patients. (VO 21) DR LETLAPE SAYS NOTHING WILL CHANGE UNTIL ALL PUBLIC SERVANTS AND POLITICIANS ARE COMPELLED TO USE STATE HEALTH CARE, RATHER THAN PRIVATE. DR KGOSI LETLAPE MP: ActionSA We can't be talking about the wage bill when the President has the temerity to go and double the size of cabinet.. …, you know, for ordinary people that are essential, that make an impact on ordinary lives, that's where we cut. But for things that are grandiose, political agreements, we will spend lavishly without any restraint. It doesn't make sense. Siviwe Gwarube Sound up: And to perform the functions of my office conscientiously and to the best of my ability… (VO 22) ONE OF THE NEWCOMERS TO CABINET IS THE MINISTER OF BASIC EDUCATION. ONCE IN OPPOSITION, SIVIWE GWARUBE IS NOW GRAPPLING WITH A MASSIVE BUDGET CRISIS JUST MONTHS INTO THE JOB. SIVIWE GWARUBE Minister for Basic Education: GNU The figure that gives me chills and and it's not a final figure, but out of about almost 118 billion rand shortfall in the next three years if the budget remains the same. PTC GOVAN WHITTLES: Ministers are lobbying the Treasury for more cash for service delivery, so there is much anticipation as this week the finance minister prepares to table his spending plan for the next three years. (VO 23) GWARUBE HAS ORGANISED MEETINGS BETWEEN PROVINCIAL EDUCATION MECs AND TREASURY TO PLEAD THE CASE FOR EDUCATION. EACH PROVINCE IS MANAGING THEIR BUDGET SHORTFALLS IN THEIR OWN WAY, BUT THIS IS A UNITED CALL FOR HELP. SIVIWE GWARUBE Minister for Basic Education: GNU My plea to Treasury is to say we need immediate buffering of the budget cuts now. (VO 24) TREASURY TOLD US THEY REGULARLY ADVISE PROVINCES ON HOW BEST TO ALLOCATE THEIR LIMITED MONEY. ALL EYES WILL BE ON THE FINANCE MINISTER THIS WEEK TO SEE WHAT HE CONCEDES WHEN HE PRESENTS HIS MEDIUM-TERM BUDGET IN PARLIAMENT. HOW WILL HE BALANCE THE NEEDS OF THE PEOPLE AGAINST THE PAY OF THE PUBLIC SERVANTS? SIVIWE GWARUBE Minister for Basic Education: GNU My view, is education, healthcare, police, service, delivery. Those are the things that are critical to any nation. So we need to have a whole review of government spending so that we can actually put our money where our mouth is. We can’t say these are priorities but then we are putting our money elsewhere. (VO 25) BUT POLITICAL TALK SEEMS CHEAP TO VENTER AND PROF MUSTAK, BOTH OF WHOM HAVE GIVEN THEIR BEST YEARS TO PUBLIC SERVICE, TO BUILD THE COUNTRY FOR GENERATIONS TO COME. PROFESSOR HAMZAH MUSTAK Ophthalmologist: Specialist in ocular oncology The wait times are what’s longer so explain that to a patient who has eye cancer or any cancer. They can lose their life. AIMEE VENTER Teacher: Natural Sciences I want other teachers to raise their voices. I want them to speak up about what is right and what is wrong. I want them to try to make a difference. ENDSIT PRESENTER LINK TO CAMERA: PROMO 1: DR KGOSI LETLAPE MP: ActionSA Our public Health care scenario has basically become a crime scene, (VO) THERE’S NONE SO BLIND AS THOSE THAT WILL NOT SEE ZADONISA MC KENZIE Patient: Groote Schuur Hospital Healthcare that is a necessity. Education is necessity. So I feel that the government is to blame big time. PROMO 2: PROFESSOR HAMZAH MUSTAK Ophthalmologist: Specialist in ocular oncology To see the service that you've built up, you know, taken apart is.. (VO) PROFESSIONALS ON THE FRONTLINE ARE UNDER PRESSURE AIMEE VENTER Teacher: Natural Sciences cutting teacher jobs is completely illogical….You are going to be constantly crowd controlling. PROMO 3: (VO) BUDGETS SLASHED, PROGRESS HALTED. DAVID MAYNIER MEC for Education: Western Cape I remember the day where.... I cancelled 11 school builds in a day. SIVIWE GWARUBE Minister for Basic Education: GNU The future of these 13 and a half million children is in jeopardy (VO) WHO WILL AUSTERITY HURT MOST? AIMEE VENTER Teacher: Natural Sciences It’s still very raw. I am still angry.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We show how national budget cuts will cripple delivery in the public service
metadata.Unique Selling Point: This is an unreported story but will have devastating consequences on the ground where people will not get services in health, education and social services as a result of the freezing of posts and the cutting of budgets which were unfunded.
metadata.Summary: The National Government concluded a wage agreement with Public Servants last year which was greater than the government could afford. As a result the treasury has passed that shortfall down to the provincial governments, so increased the wages of the civil servants but not provided the provincial paymasters with the cash to fund that increase. As a result the provinces are scrambling to cut budgets and are doing that by slashing personnel numbers, plunging service delivery into crisis. We talk to a doctor and his patients on the one hand that has been affected by this and a teacher who has lost her job and is now lost to the education system and then test their views against the political heads in the Western Cape of how they are handling it. This unreported story has been present in news pages, but because the Western Cape is the only one complaining and possibly threatening an InterGovernmental Dispute they are the canary in the coalmine in terms of what will happen in other provinces.
